_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::shell#2, and a FALSIFICATION of its premise. THICK has no default on SHELL7P — it is required:true, and omitting it is a parse error, "Required value 'THICK' not found in input line" from core/io/src/4C_io_input_spec_builders.cpp, with zero steps run. The rest of the entry stands: on a flat 8x2 SHELL7P plate, THICK 0.01 is pinned by the deck's result test and exits 0 at -2.52367752125895084e+00, while THICK 0.02 with nothing else changed gives -4.88145053467516798e-01. The fourth arm pins a naming trap between the two shell families: SHELL7P takes THICK on the element, MAT_Kirchhoff_Love_shell takes THICKNESS in the material, and writing THICKNESS on a SHELL7P line lets the parser consume the THICK prefix and then complain about the NEXT key, "Required value 'SDC' not found in input line" — a message that names a key which was never the problem. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: Required value 'THICK' not found in input line
Required value 'SDC' not found in input line

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: give the third arm its THICK key. The required-value diagnostic vanishes, NO_THICK_STEPS stops being 0 and EXIT_NO_THICK becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the second pathology: use the element-side spelling in the fourth arm. The misleading 'SDC' diagnostic vanishes and EXIT_THICKNESS becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the numeric contrast: give the second arm the reference thickness. Its answer collapses onto the pinned one and the wrong-answer line disappears, so the fixture must go red.
